summary: Kube projected serviceaccount token shadowed during vault-driven secret rotation; ephemeral runners lose auth to artifact gateway
description:
Issue summary: During an automated credential rotation (Vault AppRole + CSI driver) the projected serviceaccount token file used by ephemeral GitHub Actions runners became shadowed by a stale inode. Impact: runners intermittently fail uploads to internal artifact gateway with 401/403 during job teardown, causing archived artifacts to be missing and release pipelines to fail. Scope: ~12% of ephemeral runner pod restarts in us-east-1 across the last rotation window (2026-03-09 03:00 - 04:30 UTC).

Observed behavior: After the CSI driver rewrote secrets, the runner-agent continued running but artifact uploads to s3-gateway returned 401/unauthorized. Restarting the runner pod consistently restored uploads. No image-pull errors were observed.

Expected behavior: Rotation should atomically replace credentials such that long-lived processes either see the new token or failover gracefully; runner agents should not retain a stale token reference after a secret re-mount.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a ephemeral GH Actions runner pod with projected serviceAccountToken (k8s projected volume) and an image that uploads artifacts to internal s3-gateway.
2) Trigger Vault secret rotation for the AppRole bound to the CSI driver and let the driver re-mount the updated secret to the runner pod's projected volume.
3) Initiate a job that uploads artifacts at pod shutdown (typical release pipeline step).
4) Observe that upload returns 401/403 while runner process still runs; pod restart restores upload ability.
logs: runner-agent[2345]: INFO initiating artifact upload to s3-gateway: /artifacts/build-1234.tar.gz
runner-agent[2345]: ERROR upload failed: http status 401 Unauthorized (x-request-id: rwd-9f3b)
s3-gateway[proxy][pid=1142]: WARN auth: token validation failed: token issuer mismatch or signature invalid
kubelet[572]: INFO volumeMount: CSI driver finished write, performing remount /var/run/secrets/csi-vault/runner-tokens
kernel: inotify: watch removed (wd=102) for /var/run/secrets/csi-vault/runner-tokens/token (inode changed)
runner-agent[2345]: INFO detected token file path /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token -> inode 14576 (pre-rotation)
runner-agent[2345]: INFO token refresh check: token file inode changed to 19802 but file descriptor still points to old inode
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Vault CSI driver wrote new token with non-atomic write -> file inode changed; kubelet projected token refresh left symlink to old FD used by runner process leading to auth failures.
Confirmed with kernel audit: inotify events show remove+create semantics rather than atomic rename, so long-lived FD kept referencing removed inode.

s3-gateway logs show token validation failed with 'iss' mismatch for tokens minted during rotation window; tokens themselves were valid when read from new file but the runner process continued to use an already-open FD pointing to deleted inode containing the old token value.
Repro on staging by forcing CSI driver to write via tempfile+rename vs direct write: using tempfile+rename (atomic) removes the inode churn and prevents stale-fd reads.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Aisha Mendes (SRE): Noticed spike in failed uploads coincident with vault rotation window. Repro steps recorded in staging. Assigned to Connor Li for deeper debug.

2026-03-10 15:04 - Connor Li (Infra): Confirmed inode churn. Kubelet logs show projected token remount; runner process uses open FD and does not re-read from path when inode changes. Possible fix: ensure CSI driver uses atomic rename semantics or have kubelet propagate new token via restart or inotify-triggered reload in runner.

2026-03-11 09:23 - Diego Alvarez (Runner eng): We can add a short watcher in runner-agent to detect inode changes on token path and force token re-load; will prototype. Also raised a PR to update CSI driver write mode.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Priya Sharma (Release Eng): Workaround confirmed: restart of runner pod in failing jobs restores artifact uploads. Requesting schedule for a controlled rotation re-run with fixes in place before next release cut.
resolution: In Progress — temporary mitigation is to restart affected runner pods which forces runner-agent to re-open token file descriptor. Engineering work: (1) patch runner-agent to watch token path inode and reload token on change; (2) patch vault-csi-driver usage to perform atomic replace (tempfile + rename) when writing projected secrets; (3) coordinate with kubelet upgrade/ops to reduce remount races. Planning a controlled small-window rotation once patches are live.
recommended_fix: 1) Backport small inode-watch token reload to runner-agent (hotfix). 2) Update Vault CSI driver to write secrets atomically (tempfile + rename). 3) Add pre-rotation draining of ephemeral-runner node pool or coordinate rotation with a short runner restart wave. 4) Add automated post-rotation verification job that validates artifact upload end-to-end.
